definition: 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is usually a noun meaning a result (it can also be a verb meaning to bring about).
example: The new policy will affect everyone, but its full effect won't be clear for years.
persian: affect (فعل): تأثیر گذاشتن — effect (اسم): نتیجه/اثر

definition: 'Fewer' is for countable nouns (things you can number); 'less' is for uncountable quantities or amounts.
example: This checkout is for shoppers with fewer than ten items, so you'll spend less time waiting.
persian: fewer برای اسم‌های قابل‌شمارش (کمتر در تعداد) — less برای مقدار غیرقابل‌شمارش (کمتر در مقدار)

definition: 'Their' shows possession; 'there' refers to a place or is a dummy subject; 'they're' is the contraction of 'they are'.
example: They're putting their bags over there by the door.
persian: their: مالِ آن‌ها — there: آنجا — they're: مخففِ they are (آن‌ها هستند)

definition: 'Complement' means to complete or go well with something; 'compliment' means an expression of praise.
example: The wine complements the meal, and the chef took my compliment graciously.
persian: complement: تکمیل کردن/مکمل بودن — compliment: تعریف/تمجید

definition: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' is the contraction of 'it is' or 'it has'.
example: The dog wagged its tail because it's happy to see you.
persian: its: مالِ آن (ملکی) — it's: مخففِ it is یا it has

definition: 'Your' shows possession; 'you're' is the contraction of 'you are'.
example: You're going to need your passport at the airport.
persian: your: مالِ تو (ملکی) — you're: مخففِ you are (تو هستی)

definition: 'Accept' is a verb meaning to receive or agree to; 'except' is usually a preposition meaning excluding.
example: I accept all the terms except the last one.
persian: accept: پذیرفتن — except: به‌جز/به‌استثنای

definition: 'Then' relates to time or sequence; 'than' is used for comparisons.
example: She is taller than her brother, and back then she was even taller for her age.
persian: then: سپس/در آن زمان — than: نسبت به/از (در مقایسه)

definition: 'Lose' is a verb meaning to misplace or fail to win; 'loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.
example: If your belt is too loose, you might lose your trousers.
persian: lose (فعل): از دست دادن/باختن — loose (صفت): شل/گشاد

definition: 'Who's' is the contraction of 'who is' or 'who has'; 'whose' is the possessive form.
example: Whose coat is this, and who's going to claim it?
persian: who's: مخففِ who is/who has — whose: مالِ چه‌کسی (ملکی)

definition: 'To' is a preposition or infinitive marker; 'too' means also or excessively; 'two' is the number 2.
example: I want to come too, but two of us can't fit in the car.
persian: to: به/برای (حرف اضافه) — too: هم/خیلی زیاد — two: عددِ دو

definition: 'Principal' means main/most important, or the head of a school; 'principle' is a fundamental rule or belief.
example: The school principal explained the principal reason behind the new policy, which rests on a clear principle.
persian: principal: اصلی/مدیر مدرسه — principle: اصل/قاعده

definition: 'Stationary' means not moving; 'stationery' refers to writing materials like paper and pens.
example: The car was stationary while she bought stationery at the shop.
persian: stationary: ساکن/بی‌حرکت — stationery: لوازم‌التحریر

definition: 'Advice' is a noun (a recommendation); 'advise' is a verb (to recommend).
example: Let me advise you: the best advice I ever got was to save money.
persian: advice (اسم): نصیحت/توصیه — advise (فعل): نصیحت کردن/توصیه کردن

definition: In British English, 'practice' is the noun and 'practise' is the verb; American English uses 'practice' for both.
example: You need more practice, so practise every day.
persian: practice (اسم): تمرین — practise (فعل، بریتانیایی): تمرین کردن

definition: 'Desert' (verb) means to abandon, or (noun) a dry barren region; 'dessert' is the sweet course after a meal.
example: He would never desert his friends, even in a desert—especially before dessert.
persian: desert: بیابان/ترک کردن — dessert: دسر

definition: 'Breath' is a noun (the air you take in); 'breathe' is a verb (the act of taking air in and out).
example: Take a deep breath and breathe slowly.
persian: breath (اسم): نفس — breathe (فعل): نفس کشیدن

definition: 'Emigrate' means to leave one's own country to settle elsewhere; 'immigrate' means to come into a new country to live.
example: They emigrated from Iran in 1990 and immigrated to Canada the same year.
persian: emigrate: مهاجرت کردن از کشور خود — immigrate: مهاجرت کردن به کشوری دیگر

definition: 'Assure' means to reassure a person; 'ensure' means to make certain; 'insure' means to protect with an insurance policy.
example: I assure you we'll ensure the goods are insured before shipping.
persian: assure: اطمینان دادن (به کسی) — ensure: مطمئن ساختن — insure: بیمه کردن

definition: 'Lay' means to put something down and takes an object; 'lie' means to recline and takes no object.
example: Lay the book on the table, then lie down for a nap.
persian: lay: گذاشتن چیزی (مفعول می‌گیرد) — lie: دراز کشیدن (مفعول نمی‌گیرد)

definition: 'Farther' refers to physical distance; 'further' refers to figurative or additional degree/extent.
example: We walked farther down the road and decided to discuss it no further.
persian: farther: دورتر (مسافت فیزیکی) — further: بیشتر/علاوه بر این (مجازی)

definition: Use 'between' for two distinct items or one-to-one relationships; use 'among' for three or more as a group.
example: Split the prize between the two winners, and share the snacks among all the guests.
persian: between: میانِ دو چیز — among: میانِ سه چیز یا بیشتر

definition: 'e.g.' means 'for example' and introduces examples; 'i.e.' means 'that is' and introduces a clarification or restatement.
example: Bring a warm layer, e.g. a jumper; wear it indoors, i.e. inside the building.
persian: e.g.: مثلاً/برای مثال — i.e.: یعنی/به عبارت دیگر

definition: 'Council' is a noun meaning an official group or assembly; 'counsel' means advice, or to advise (also a lawyer).
example: The city council met to counsel residents on the new rules.
persian: council: شورا/انجمن — counsel: مشاوره/نصیحت کردن

definition: 'Elicit' is a verb meaning to draw out a response; 'illicit' is an adjective meaning illegal or forbidden.
example: The detective tried to elicit a confession about the illicit deal.
persian: elicit: استخراج کردن/بیرون کشیدن (پاسخ) — illicit: غیرقانونی/ممنوع

definition: An 'allusion' is an indirect reference; an 'illusion' is a false impression or deceptive appearance.
example: Her speech made an allusion to a famous poem, creating the illusion of deep wisdom.
persian: allusion: اشاره/کنایه — illusion: توهم/پندار باطل

definition: 'Discreet' means careful or tactful about keeping things private; 'discrete' means separate and distinct.
example: Be discreet about the news; there are three discrete stages to the plan.
persian: discreet: محتاط/رازدار — discrete: مجزا/جداگانه

definition: 'Cite' means to quote or refer to a source; 'site' is a location; 'sight' relates to vision or something seen.
example: Cite your sources on the website, then visit the building site to see the sight.
persian: cite: ارجاع دادن/نقل کردن — site: مکان/سایت — sight: دید/منظره

definition: 'Capital' means the chief city, money/assets, or an uppercase letter; 'capitol' is specifically the building where a legislature meets.
example: Lawmakers gathered at the capitol in the state capital to debate raising capital.
persian: capital: پایتخت/سرمایه/حرف بزرگ — capitol: ساختمان مجلس/کنگره

definition: 'Bear' means to carry or endure (or the animal); 'bare' means uncovered or to expose.
example: I can't bear to look at the bare walls of the empty room.
persian: bear: تحمل کردن/حمل کردن (یا خرس) — bare: لخت/برهنه/آشکار کردن

definition: 'Weather' refers to atmospheric conditions; 'whether' introduces a choice or alternative (like 'if').
example: I'm not sure whether the weather will hold for the picnic.
persian: weather: آب‌وهوا — whether: آیا/خواه (برای انتخاب)

definition: 'Passed' is the past tense of the verb 'pass'; 'past' refers to a previous time, or means beyond.
example: We passed the old school as we drove past it, remembering the past.
persian: passed: گذشتِ فعلِ pass (عبور کرد) — past: گذشته/ماورای

definition: 'Comprise' means to include or consist of (the whole comprises the parts); 'compose' means to make up (the parts compose the whole).
example: The team comprises ten players, and ten players compose the team.
persian: comprise: شامل بودن/تشکیل شدن از — compose: تشکیل دادن

definition: 'Continual' means repeated with breaks in between; 'continuous' means uninterrupted, without any pause.
example: There were continual interruptions all morning, then a continuous hum from the machine all afternoon.
persian: continual: مکرر (با وقفه) — continuous: پیوسته/بی‌وقفه

definition: 'Imply' means to suggest something without saying it directly (the speaker implies); 'infer' means to deduce it (the listener infers).
example: Her tone implied she was upset, so I inferred that I'd said something wrong.
persian: imply: تلویحاً بیان کردن (گوینده) — infer: استنباط کردن (شنونده)

definition: 'Economic' relates to the economy or finance; 'economical' means thrifty, giving good value, not wasteful.
example: The economic crisis forced families to be more economical with food.
persian: economic: اقتصادی (مربوط به اقتصاد) — economical: مقرون‌به‌صرفه/صرفه‌جو

definition: 'Historic' means famous or important in history; 'historical' means relating to the past or to history in general.
example: The signing was a historic moment, recorded in many historical documents.
persian: historic: تاریخی (مهم/ماندگار) — historical: تاریخی (مربوط به گذشته)

definition: 'Loath' is an adjective meaning reluctant or unwilling; 'loathe' is a verb meaning to hate intensely.
example: I'm loath to admit it, but I loathe getting up early.
persian: loath (صفت): بی‌میل/اکراه‌داشته — loathe (فعل): متنفر بودن

definition: 'Precede' means to come before something; 'proceed' means to go forward or continue.
example: A short introduction will precede the talk, and then we'll proceed to questions.
persian: precede: مقدم بودن/پیش از آمدن — proceed: ادامه دادن/پیش رفتن

definition: 'Dependent' is an adjective meaning relying on something/someone; 'dependant' (British) is a noun for a person who depends on you.
example: The outcome is dependent on the weather, and he has three dependants to support.
persian: dependent (صفت): وابسته — dependant (اسم، بریتانیایی): فردِ تحت تکفل

definition: 'Lead' (present tense, rhymes with 'feed') means to guide; 'led' is its past tense. ('Lead' as a metal rhymes with 'red'.)
example: She will lead the team this year, just as she led them last year.
persian: lead (حال): هدایت کردن — led (گذشته): هدایت کرد

definition: 'Flaunt' means to show off ostentatiously; 'flout' means to openly disregard or defy a rule.
example: He likes to flaunt his wealth, and he flouts the parking rules every day.
persian: flaunt: به‌رخ کشیدن/خودنمایی کردن — flout: نادیده گرفتن/زیر پا گذاشتن (قانون)

definition: 'Prescribe' means to recommend or order (e.g. medicine or a rule); 'proscribe' means to forbid or ban.
example: The doctor prescribed rest, while the law proscribes smoking indoors.
persian: prescribe: تجویز کردن/مقرر کردن — proscribe: ممنوع/تحریم کردن

definition: 'Adverse' means harmful or unfavourable (usually of conditions); 'averse' means strongly opposed or disinclined (of a person).
example: Despite adverse weather, she wasn't averse to a long walk.
persian: adverse: نامساعد/زیان‌آور — averse: بیزار/مخالف

definition: 'Censor' means to suppress or remove objectionable parts; 'censure' means to criticize or condemn formally.
example: The board voted to censure the official after he tried to censor the report.
persian: censor: سانسور کردن — censure: نکوهش/توبیخ رسمی

definition: 'Defuse' means to calm or remove danger from a situation; 'diffuse' means to spread out, or (adjective) spread thin and unfocused.
example: She managed to defuse the argument before the tension could diffuse through the office.
persian: defuse: خنثی/آرام کردن — diffuse: پخش/منتشر شدن

definition: 'Complementary' means combining well to form a whole; 'complimentary' means given free, or expressing praise.
example: The two colours are complementary, and the hotel offered a complimentary breakfast.
persian: complementary: مکمل/تکمیل‌کننده — complimentary: رایگان/تحسین‌آمیز

definition: 'Everyday' (one word) is an adjective meaning ordinary or routine; 'every day' (two words) is an adverb phrase meaning each day.
example: Brushing your teeth is an everyday task that you should do every day.
persian: everyday (صفت): روزمره/معمولی — every day (قید): هر روز

definition: 'Sensual' relates to physical, often sexual, gratification; 'sensuous' relates to pleasure of the senses more broadly (art, beauty, sound).
example: The dance was openly sensual, while the music was richly sensuous.
persian: sensual: شهوانی/جسمانی — sensuous: لذت‌بخش برای حواس (هنری/زیبایی‌شناختی)
